findings.title: Monochrome conservation shading never reads the consensus string, so the U change cannot desync "differs from consensus" shading
findings.reasoning: applyConservationShadeClass compares the row's uppercased residue with posData.consensusBases, and those sets are built fresh from the row letters in _computeConservationForColumn (9716-9730, line 9730 "    for (const c of order) if (buf[c] === maxCount) consensusBases.add(String.fromCharCode(c));") with uppercasing at 9720 ("        if (c >= 97 && c <= 122) c -= 32;"). The consensus string from computeConsensusForSequences is never an input here, so v333's U change does not affect this path; row 'u' and consensus char 'U' are both produced by the same row-side normalization.
findings.scenario: RNA alignment, monochrome scheme, conservation sliders on: residues equal to the column majority shade black/dark/light exactly as before v333, U or T alike.

findings.title: Colour-table lookup for a U residue gets the same class keys as T ('base-U' letter class + pyrimidine group)
findings.reasoning: getResidueAnnotationClasses (14163) uppercases first (14164 "    const baseUp = String(base || '-').toUpperCase();"), pushes the per-letter colour key at 14169 ("        classes.push(`base-${baseUp}`);") for any single A-Z letter including U, and explicitly maps U into the same pyrimidine group as T at 14190. So a consensus char 'U' and a row char 'T' receive pyrimidine group class on both sides; the only asymmetry is the base-* letter class name itself (base-U vs base-T), which is a consistent rename, not a half-mapped comparison, for U-residue columns. I did not get to read RESIDUE_SCHEME_STYLES to verify a 'base-U' entry exists in every nucleotide palette; if some palette only defines keys under class priority names it could miss a styled colour for U, so that sub-case remains unverified.
findings.scenario: Consensus inserted as a row in an RNA alignment, any colour scheme: each U residue classifies as pyrimidine like T, and GET_ENTRY standard/ambiguous letter classes (line 14179) treat it as a known nucleotide.

findings.title: A consensus row made of U letters cannot flip the alignment into "protein" mode
findings.reasoning: _alignmentLooksProtein (14097) counts a nucleotide-alignment consensus row's U's as nucleotide letters because the Uint8Array marks uppercase and lowercase U; combined with the >10%-other test at 14109 ("    return letters > 0 && other / letters > 0.1;") an inserted consensus row (a computeConsensusForSequences caller) of A/C/G/U/gaps leaves the alignment nucleotide-type, so colour-scheme remapping at 14131 ("    if (isProteinAlignment() && NUCLEOTIDE_ORIENTED_SCHEMES.has(scheme)) {") is not triggered by the new U characters.
findings.scenario: RNA alignment with 'Insert consensus as sequence': the alignment is not reclassified as protein and nucleotide colour schemes are kept.

findings.title: Consensus char path maps U->T before counting (4598) but the conservation-shading path counts U and T as distinct letters, so a mixed U/T RNA column can shade the inserted consensus row as a mismatch
findings.reasoning: The consensus decision folds U into T: line 4598 "        if (!isProtein && c === 85) c = 84;          // U -> T" and _getConsensusOptions sets isRna (line 4550 "        isRna: _alignmentIsRnaCached(),   // an RNA alignment gets its consensus in U (audit 2026-11-10, H8)"), so an RNA column of mixed T and u letters yields consensus char 'U'. But _computeConservationForColumn (9711-9737) has no U/T folding (its only skip is the quoted line 9723), so consensusBases at line 9730 contains only 'T' when T is the majority. The consensus row inserted as a sequence then fails the equality test at 14217 ("posData.consensusBases?.has(baseUp)") for its own U residues: every U of the consensus row renders in the 'other'/mismatch shade in monochrome mode instead of the conserved shade, because one side of the comparison folds U/T together (4598) and the other (9723/9730) does not.
findings.scenario: Load an RNA alignment detected as RNA by alignmentIsRna() where some rows still hold DNA-style T (mixed U/T input). Shade mode monochrome, insert the consensus as a sequence (a computeConsensusForSequences caller). The consensus row's U letters, which the row-side consensus fold produced from the very same rows, are shaded as differing from the column consensus while the T rows shade as matching - the inserted consensus looks like a mismatch row against its own definition.

note: Audited the consensus-U consumers I could trace within the reading budget. Key results: (1) conservation/monochrome "differs from consensus" shading is built entirely from row letters (_computeConservationForColumn, script.js 9711-9737) and never reads the consensus string, so v333's U change cannot desynchronize it (ok, line 14217); (2) colour-class lookup in getResidueAnnotationClasses uppercases both sides and maps U into the same pyrimidine group as T (lines 14164/14169/14190) — base-U vs base-T letter keys are a consistent rename (ok), though I could not verify that every RESIDUE_SCHEME_STYLES palette defines a U entry for the value case; (3) a U consensus row cannot flip the alignment to protein because _NUCLEOTIDE_LETTER marks u/U as nucleotides (line 14096); (4) low-confidence defect: the consensus decision folds U->T (line 4598) and back to U via isRna, while the conservation path counts U and T as distinct letters (9723/9730), so in a mixed U/T RNA alignment the inserted consensus row's own U letters shade as mismatches (line 9723 quoted). Unverified within the remaining budget: the dot-plot consensus comparison (_dotConsPrivate ~34480), realign-against-consensus, identity-to-consensus stats and export consumers (callers at 12884, 13854, 17667-17894, 19419, 23015, 26763, 30223-30471, 33866, 34488) — I ran out of read budget before reaching them and have not claimed anything about them.
